**आपकी स्थिति का संक्षिप्त विवरण:**
आपने 12 अगस्त 2026 को स्मार्टकार्ट (SmartCart) वेबसाइट से ₹15,000 का टीवी खरीदा, जो टूटा हुआ मिला। आपने उसी दिन ई-मेल करके वापसी (रिफंड) की माँग की, लेकिन कंपनी पैसे वापस करने से मना कर रही है। आपके पास बिल और टूटे टीवी की तस्वीरें हैं।

---

**कानून क्या कहता है:**

- **खराबी (Defect) की परिभाषा:** कानून के तहत, सामान की गुणवत्ता में कोई भी fault या खराबी "डिफेक्ट" मानी जाती है।
- **सामान वापस लेने और रिफंड देने से मना न करना:** ऑनलाइन विक्रेता (Seller) खराब या टूटे हुए सामान को वापस लेने या पैसे लौटाने से इनकार नहीं कर सकता।
- **अनुचित व्यापार व्यवहार (Unfair Trade Practice):** सामान बेचने के बाद खराब सामान वापस लेने या बिल/रसीद में तय समय सीमा (या समय सीमा तय न होने पर 30 दिनों के भीतर) पैसे वापस करने से मना करना अनुचित व्यापार व्यवहार माना जाता है।
- **शिकायत अधिकारी की जिम्मेदारी:** ई-कॉमर्स प्लेटफॉर्म के ग्रीवेंस ऑफिसर (Grievance Officer) को शिकायत मिलने के 48 घंटों के भीतर रसीद देनी होती है और 1 महीने के भीतर शिकायत का समाधान करना होता है।
- **विक्रेता (Seller) की जानकारी माँगना:** यदि आपको सेलर का ब्योरा चाहिए, तो आप प्लेटफॉर्म से लिखित में विक्रेता की जानकारी माँग सकते हैं।
- **उपभोक्ता आयोग और मुआवजा:** आप जिला उपभोक्ता आयोग (District Commission) में शिकायत दर्ज करा सकते हैं। ₹5 लाख तक के दावों के लिए आयोग में कोई कोर्ट फीस (Nil) नहीं लगती है। शिकायत सही साबित होने पर आयोग पैसे वापस करने, सामान बदलने या हर्जाना देने का आदेश दे सकता है।

---

**आपके व्यावहारिक विकल्प:**

1. **ग्रीवेंस ऑफिसर को औपचारिक शिकायत:** स्मार्टकार्ट के शिकायत अधिकारी (Grievance Officer) को ईमेल भेजें और नियमों के तहत 1 महीने में समाधान माँगें।
2. **राष्ट्रीय उपभोक्ता हेल्पलाइन (NCH):** आप अपनी शिकायत उपभोक्ता हेल्पलाइन पोर्टल [consumerhelpline.gov.in](https://consumerhelpline.gov.in) पर दर्ज कर सकते हैं।
3. **उपभोक्ता आयोग में ऑनलाइन शिकायत:** यदि समस्या हल नहीं होती, तो आप [e-jagriti.gov.in](https://e-jagriti.gov.in) पर जाकर जिला आयोग में ई-फाइलिंग (ऑनलाइन शिकायत) दर्ज कर सकते हैं।

---

**क्या अनिश्चित है (अधूरी जानकारी):**
- यह स्पष्ट नहीं है कि टीवी खोलते समय आपके पास कोई अनबॉक्सिंग वीडियो (Unboxing Video) है या केवल तस्वीरें हैं।
- क्या कंपनी की तरफ से मना करने का कोई लिखित कारण (ई-मेल) दिया गया है, यह जानकारी अभी उपलब्ध नहीं है।

*यह केवल कानूनी जानकारी है और इसे कानूनी सलाह न माना जाए। अपने मामले की विशेष सलाह के लिए किसी योग्य वकील से परामर्श करें।*

steps.title: 1. सभी दस्तावेज और सबूत एकत्र करें
steps.detail: आपके पास SmartCart का बिल और टूटे हुए TV की तस्वीरें पहले से मौजूद हैं। यदि आपके पास अनबॉक्सिंग (सामान खोलते समय का) वीडियो या कंपनी द्वारा रिफंड से इनकार करने वाला कोई लिखित ईमेल है, तो उसे भी संभाल कर रखें।

steps.title: 2. SmartCart के ग्रीवांस ऑफिसर (शिकायत अधिकारी) को औपचारिक शिकायत भेजें

steps.title: 3. राष्ट्रीय उपभोक्ता हेल्पलाइन (NCH) में शिकायत दर्ज कराएं

steps.title: 4. जिला उपभोक्ता कमीशन में शिकायत दर्ज करने पर विचार करें

- **खराबी (Defect) की परिभाषा:** कानून के तहत, सामान की गुणवत्ता में कोई भी fault या खराबी "डिफेक्ट" मानी जाती है [SRC:CPA2019-S2-10]।

FACT RULES.
- Use only facts the user actually gave. Never invent dates, amounts, names, conversations or evidence.
- If a detail is missing, say it is missing. Do not guess it.

STYLE.
- Write for someone who has never dealt with a legal matter. Use short sentences and everyday words.
- If you must use a legal term, explain it in the same sentence.

- recipient must describe the correct recipient for this document type, using a placeholder for any unknown name or address.

Write the document in English, unless the user's note asks otherwise.

VERIFIED SOURCES:
[SRC:CPA2019-S2-47-viii]
Source: Section 2(47)(viii), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof, if paid, within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days
Plain explanation: Refusing to take back defective goods, or to stop deficient services, and refund the money is listed as an unfair trade practice. The time limit is the period stated in the bill or receipt. If none is stated, it is thirty days.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R6-3]
Source: Rule 6(3), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: No seller offering goods or services through a marketplace e -commerce entity shall refuse to take back goods, or withdraw or discontinue services purchased or agreed to be purchased, or refuse to refund consideration, if paid, if such goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or if the goods or services are not of the characteristics or features as advertised or as agreed to, or if such goods or services are delivered late from the stated delivery schedule | Provided that in the case of late delivery, this sub -rule shall not be applied if such late delivery was due to force majeure
Plain explanation: A marketplace seller must not refuse to take back goods or refund the money if the goods or services are defective, deficient, spurious, different from what was advertised or agreed, or delivered late. Late delivery caused by force majeure is an exception.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R2-1]
Source: Rule 2(1), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: all goods and services bought or sold over digital or electronic network including digital products | all models of e-commerce, including marketplace and inventory models of e-commerce
Plain explanation: The E-Commerce Rules apply to goods and services bought or sold online, including digital products, and to both marketplace and inventory models.

[SRC:CPA2019-S2-11]
Source: Section 2(11), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: “deficiency” means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service
Plain explanation: A deficiency is a fault or inadequacy in how a service is performed, measured against what the law requires or what the provider undertook to do. Failing to deliver a promised service may fall within this meaning, depending on the facts.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R4-10]
Source: Rule 4(10), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Every e-commerce entity shall effect all payments towards accepted refund requests of the consumers as prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India or any other competent authority under any law for the time being in force, within a reasonable period of time, or as prescribed under applicable laws
Plain explanation: Once a refund request is accepted, an online platform must pay it within a reasonable time, or within the time set by the Reserve Bank of India or other applicable law. This rule does not itself state a fixed number of days.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R4-4]
Source: Rule 4(4), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Every e-commerce entity shall establish an adequate grievance redressal mechanism having regard to the number of grievances ordinarily received by such entity from India, and shall appoint a grievance officer for consumer grievance redressal, and shall display the name, contact details, and designation of such officer on its platform
Plain explanation: Every online platform must have a way to handle complaints and must appoint a grievance officer, whose name, contact details and designation must be displayed on the platform. This is often where a written complaint can be sent first.

[SRC:CPA2019-S37-1]
Source: Section 37(1), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: if it appears to the District Commission that there exists elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties, except in such cases as may be prescribed, it may direct the parties to give in writing, within five days, consent to have their dispute settled by mediation
Plain explanation: If a settlement looks possible, the District Commission may ask both sides whether they agree in writing to try mediation. Some cases are excluded.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R5-3-b]
Source: Rule 5(3)(b), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: a ticket number for each complaint lodged through which the consumer can track the status of the complaint
Plain explanation: A marketplace must provide a ticket number for each complaint, so the consumer can track its status. Keep this number as evidence.

[SRC:JUR2021-R3]
Source: Rule 3, Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021, G.S.R. 912(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees
Plain explanation: The District Commission hears complaints where the amount paid for the goods or services is up to fifty lakh rupees. This replaced the higher limit originally written in section 34 of the Act.

[SRC:CPA2019-S39-1]
Source: Section 39(1), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: to return to the complainant the price, or, as the case may be, the charges paid by the complainant along with such interest on such price or charges as may be decided | to replace the goods with new goods of similar description which shall be free from any defect | to remove the defects in goods or deficiencies in the services in question | to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation to the consumer for any loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to the negligence of the opposite party | to provide for adequate costs to parties
Plain explanation: If the complaint is proved, the Commission can order remedies such as repair, replacement, a refund with interest, compensation for loss caused by negligence, and costs. What it actually orders depends on the case.

[SRC:EJAGRITI-LIMITATION-DOCS]
Source: e-Jagriti: Consumer Complaint (CC) Workflow: Consumer Complaint workflow
Status: In force.
Official wording: Mandatory Documents -Index -Proforma for Filing CC -Synopsis with List of Dates and Events -Memo of Parties -CC with Notarised affidavit -Add Annexures / Documents -Add Application (IA) -Vakalatnama | Filed within the period of 2 Yrs of cause of action
Plain explanation: The official e-Jagriti workflow lists the documents for filing a consumer complaint, including a synopsis with dates and events, a memo of parties and a notarised affidavit. Check the portal's current list, because it may change.

[SRC:CDRC2023-R7-FEE]
Source: Rule 7, Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) (Amendment) Rules, 2023, G.S.R. 606(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Upto Rupees Five Lakh Nil | Above Rupees Five Lakh and upto Rupees Ten Lakh Rs. 200 | Above Rupees Ten Lakh and upto Rupees Twenty Lakh Rs. 400 | Above Rupees Twenty Lakh and upto Rupees Fifty Lakh Rs. 1000 | Above Rupees Fifty Lakh and upto Rupees One Crore Rs. 2000 | Above Rupees One Crore and upto Rupees Two Crore Rs. 2500
Plain explanation: The filing fee depends on the amount paid for the goods or services: no fee up to Rs. 5 lakh, Rs. 200 up to Rs. 10 lakh, Rs. 400 up to Rs. 20 lakh, Rs. 1,000 up to Rs. 50 lakh, Rs. 2,000 up to Rs. 1 crore and Rs. 2,500 up to Rs. 2 crore. Higher bands are in the rule. Check the fee shown on e-Jagriti before filing.

[SRC:CPA2019-S69]
Source: Section 69, The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen | a complaint may be entertained after the period specified in sub -section ( 1), if the complainant satisfies the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, that he had sufficient cause for not filing the complaint within such period
Plain explanation: A complaint must generally be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arose. A late complaint may be accepted only if the Commission is satisfied there was sufficient cause for the delay. Working out the start date can be difficult, so check it with a lawyer if time may be short.

[SRC:NCH-CONTACT]
Source: National Consumer Helpline: official website: Helpline contact details
Status: In force.
Official wording: Toll Free 1915 (8AM to 8PM) | WhatsApp +918800001915 | Call National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or 1800114000 | Register your consumer grievance through the NCH Web Portal, Mobile App, UMANG, WhatsApp or Call Centre.
Plain explanation: The National Consumer Helpline can be reached on toll-free 1915 (8 AM to 8 PM) or 1800114000, or on WhatsApp at +918800001915. A grievance can be registered through its web portal, mobile app, UMANG, WhatsApp or call centre.

[SRC:CPA2019-S35-1]
Source: Section 35(1), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Provided that the complaint under this sub -section may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed | A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by
Plain explanation: A consumer can file a complaint about goods or services with a District Commission, and the Act allows complaints to be filed electronically.
